issues.description: The problem statement instructs students to use a predefined variable named `greetingText` for output, but both the template and the solution define and use a variable named `hello` (no `greetingText` exists). This name mismatch can confuse students about which variable to use and where to make their changes.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the variable name consistent across all artifacts. Either update the problem statement to refer to the predefined `hello` variable, or change the template and solution to define and use `greetingText` (e.g. `greetingText db "Hello World!", 10, 0`) so the name in the instructions matches the code.

issues.description: The problem statement tells students to use a predefined variable named `greetingText` for output, but both the template and the solution define and use a variable named `hello` (e.g., `hello db "Hello World!"` and `push hello`). This mismatch means a student following the problem text will look for `greetingText` in the starter code and not find it, creating unnecessary confusion and extra work to map the intended output variable to the actual identifier in the code.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the identifier consistent across artifacts. Either (A) change the variable name in template_repository/helloWorld.asm and solution_repository/helloWorld.asm from `hello` to `greetingText` (update the label and all uses, e.g., `push greetingText`), or (B) update the problem statement to reference `hello` instead of `greetingText`. Choice (A) is preferable to match the problem text while keeping the variable name descriptive.
